samuel2.6.p1.b1.text: David again assembled the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand in all. … set out for Baale of Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, …

samuel2.6.p1.b2.text: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, … Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart

samuel2.6.p1.b3.text: David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.

samuel2.6.p2.b1.text: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen had stumbled.

samuel2.6.p2.b2.text: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.

samuel2.6.p2.b3.text: Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah; so he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.

samuel2.6.p3.b1.text: How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?

samuel2.6.p3.b2.text: So he was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

samuel2.6.p3.b3.text: Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household.

samuel2.6.p4.b1.text: The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.

samuel2.6.p4.b2.text: So David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing.

samuel2.6.p4.b3.text: When those carrying the ark of the LORD had advanced six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.

samuel2.6.p5.b1.text: And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD,

samuel2.6.p5.b2.text: … brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sounding of the ram’s horn.

samuel2.6.p6.b1.text: As the ark of the LORD was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.

samuel2.6.p6.b2.text: So they brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it.

samuel2.6.p7.b1.text: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.

samuel2.6.p7.b2.text: Then he distributed to every man and woman among the multitude of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.

samuel2.6.p7.b3.text: And all the people departed, each for his own home.

samuel2.6.p8.b1.text: How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today! … He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, …

samuel2.6.p8.b2.text: I was dancing before the LORD, … I will celebrate before the LORD, …

samuel2.6.p8.b3.text: and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this.

samuel2.6.p8.b4.text: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.
